description: Cases for the anomaly-scoring and missing-data evaluators. Baseline samples are generated from the seeded recipes below rather than stored as tens of thousands of literals: the recipe is the versioned artefact, and it reproduces the same floats on every machine because the generators use only random.Random(seed).random() plus arithmetic, never a library distribution whose implementation may change. Changing any 'sample' block, 'observed' rule or 'expect' block is a dataset change and requires bumping dataset_version.
notes: n = 450 is what the real pipeline sees: a 15-day seasonal window over a 30-year reference period.

'observed' is expressed as a rule against the generated sample wherever the point of the case is a position in the distribution (the sample maximum, the fifth-largest value, the 90th percentile). Hard-coding a float there would have hidden the intent and broken silently if a recipe were ever retuned.
Distribution parameters are plausible rather than fitted. No case claims to describe a real city, and no number here is presented as a measurement.

cases.title: Warm but unremarkable daily maximum
A completely ordinary day, which must not reach the board
cases.note: The single most important negative case in the set. A median day scores about 0.30, under the 0.5 publication floor, so the ranking is not merely ordering noise on quiet days — it declines to publish it.

cases.title: Unusually warm overnight minimum
Cold anomaly, exercising the lower tail
cases.note: Temperature is two-tailed: a cold day is as much an outlier as a hot one, and must be scored on the same scale rather than discarded.

cases.title: Heavy rain in a climate that rains often
Strong gust, upper tail only
cases.note: Gusts are right-skewed, so a z-score is reported for familiarity but must be flagged as not comparable across metrics.

cases.title: Exactly equals the reference-period maximum
cases.note: The probability floor binds here, so the published figure is a bound and the prose must say 'at least this rare'. The margin term is zero because the value ties the record rather than clearing it.

cases.title: Clears the reference-period maximum outright
cases.note: Same floored probability as the case above, so only the margin term separates them. That is the whole reason the margin term exists.

cases.title: Colder than anything in the reference sample
Sits exactly on the retained-tail boundary
cases.note: Production keeps the five most extreme order statistics verbatim, so at the fifth the sketch is still lossless and agreement with the reference must be exact.

cases.title: One step inside the sketch's interpolated region
cases.note: The companion to the case above, and the reason this suite reports a measured sketch discrepancy instead of asserting zero everywhere. Here the sketch interpolates across a grid gap, so a small difference from the exact-sample reference is correct behaviour, not a defect.

cases.title: Degenerate baseline: every reference value identical
cases.note: IQR and standard deviation are both zero, so the margin has no scale to be expressed in and must degrade to zero rather than dividing by it. Physically implausible; arithmetically reachable, which is what matters.

cases.title: Heavy rain where it almost never rains
cases.note: The case the zero-inflated mixture exists for. Treated as one continuous variable, the dry mass would drag the estimate and badly understate how unusual this is.

cases.title: A dry day is not an upper-tail event
cases.note: Dry spells are a multi-day question and out of scope for a daily metric, so zero rainfall is excluded by name rather than scored as a lower-tail outlier.

cases.title: No cached baseline for this city, metric and day
cases.note: Must produce an inspectable exclusion, not a silent drop and not a score computed against nothing.

cases.title: Baseline row exists but its sample is empty
Too few reference values to estimate a tail
cases.note: 100 < the 120-sample floor. The value would score highly if scored, which is exactly why the gate has to come first.

cases.title: Enough values, drawn from too few years
cases.note: Sample count alone is not enough: 450 values from 10 years cannot resolve a 1-in-30-year tail, however many of them there are.

cases.title: Almost no wet days in the reference window
cases.note: Expects 'insufficient_baseline' rather than 'insufficient_wet_days' on purpose. The baseline builder folds the wet-day floor into the 'sufficient' flag, so that broader gate fires first. Recorded as observed behaviour, not asserted as the nicer of the two names.

cases.title: Wet-day floor raised above the value used when the baseline was built
cases.note: The only route by which 'insufficient_wet_days' is reachable, and the reason it is still worth having: a caller that demands a stricter floor than the stored baseline was built to must be refused rather than served.

cases.title: Observation absent
cases.note: Nothing to score, so nothing is returned — as distinct from a baseline problem, which produces a named exclusion.

cases.title: Observation is NaN
cases.note: A NaN that reached the scorer would propagate through every comparison and silently sort anywhere, so it has to be refused at the door.

cases.title: Scores just under the publication floor
